universal_lens: The exact win-probability process constitutes a discrete-time martingale over the Markovian state space. Structural rigidity enforces probability conservation, while hierarchical shrinkage and exponential recency weighting resolve non-stationary scoring drifts without violating the fundamental backward-induction recursion. The calibration-leverage tradeoff manifests as a structural isomorphism between backward induction on Markovian state spaces and conformal prediction under conditional dependence. When one-ball marginals are exactly calibrated, the residual win-probability error strictly bounds the unmodeled temporal autocorrelation of latent momentum.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the estimation layer to a conformal Bayesian hierarchy. Dirichlet pseudo-counts enforce strict calibration across sparse outcome cells, while rolling-origin cross-validation on exponentially weighted data guarantees robust predictive intervals under severe distribution shifts in modern T20 scoring rates. GSI maps this by treating the exact one-ball marginals as the conformal baseline. The systematic deviation in win probability serves as a non-conformity score, isolating the latent innings-level heterogeneity from short-range momentum via permutation null distributions.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes the exact backward sweep to compute instantaneous leverage (Leverage Index). By isolating high-leverage state transitions, GSE identifies structural performance cliffs, mapping raw run-scoring events directly to their true probabilistic impact on match resolution. GSE utilizes the verified marginals to construct a base-state transition matrix. The identified lag-1 to lag-5 autocorrelation dictates dynamic state-augmentation, allowing the engine to modulate leverage calculations when short-range momentum violates strict Markovian independence.
